events.title: The excommunication of Martin Luther
events.shortBlurb: By the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, Pope Leo X formally excommunicated Martin Luther, sealing the breach of the Reformation…
body: On 3 January 1521 Pope Leo X issued the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, which carried into effect the excommunication threatened the previous year in Exsurge Domine. Luther had publicly burned that earlier warning along with books of canon law, and having refused to retract his condemned propositions, he was now cut off from the communion of the Church.

The sentence did not end the movement but hardened it. A few months later Luther stood before the emperor and the imperial Diet at Worms and again refused to recant, and the definitive rupture of Western Christendom was underway.
